The Medical Assistant reflects the mission, vision, and values of Northwestern Medicine, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

The Medical Assistant is a member of the health care team primarily responsible for providing support to physicians, nurses, and other licensed medical staff by facilitating efficient patient flow, assisting with various patient care activities, and performing related administrative functions. The Medical Assistant is responsible for ensuring efficient patient flow through the clinic; maintaining neat, clean and safe patient care areas; promoting patient satisfaction by interacting with patients in a professional, friendly manner; safeguarding patient confidentiality.

jobs.title: Paid Social Manager

At Pair Eyewear, we believe in placing our people at the center of everything we do. We are dedicated to fostering a joyful and dynamic workplace, providing our employees with an environment where they can thrive and make a meaningful impact.



Pair is seeking a Paid Social Manager to own and scale our paid social presence across Meta, TikTok, and emerging platforms. This role will report to our Director of Growth & VP of Marketing. You'll have the opportunity to make a big impact on one of our fastest-growing revenue-driving channels in an incredibly collaborative, high-growth environment.

Your partners will span marketing, product, data & analytics, and creative with real ownership over both the strategy and day-to-day execution. That means going deep on full-funnel campaign strategy, creative testing, measurement rigor, and channel expansion with the primary focus of driving efficient new customer growth.

What You'll Do

Strategy, Execution & Measurement

 - Develop and execute full-funnel paid social strategies across Meta, TikTok, and additional channels that balance brand storytelling with performance objectives

 - Own budget pacing and bid strategy management across campaigns, allocating spend dynamically based on where we see the most efficient incremental returns

 - Establish a strong POV on retargeting frameworks due to Pair’s long lead to purchase journey with the goal of improving conversion rates and customer lifetime value

 - Partner with our data & analytics team on attribution models, incrementality testing, and Leads/CPA measurement — able to pressure-test what actually drove performance before scaling

 - Define tactic-level KPIs and build actionable reporting for leadership and cross-functional stakeholders

Creative & Testing

 - Collaborate with our Creative team to own our testing roadmap end-to-end — standing up process and ops for generating new content regularly and building durable test plans the team can reuse

 - Partner closely with our creative team to develop high-performing, platform-native content, using performance data to inform briefs and influence what gets made

 - Leverage AI tools to accelerate creative experimentation with the goal of expanding test velocity

 - Partner with other teams to identify landing page friction points across Paid Social and own the testing roadmap

Channel Growth

 - Own sophisticated audience targeting frameworks across Meta and TikTok, sustaining results through platform shifts and stagnant performance

 - Identify opportunities to scale emerging channels, beta products, and innovative media formats (Snap, Pinterest, AppLovin, Reddit, and beyond)

 - Stay ahead of platform changes — privacy updates, AI bidding shifts, new ad formats — and proactively evolve strategy in response

 - Partner cross-functionally with creative, product, CRM, and data & analytics teams to align paid social efforts with broader business objectives and campaign moments

Who You Are

 - You're a full-stack paid social operator who owns the channel with confidence — strategy, execution, creative, and measurement

 - You balance analytical rigor with creative intuition, knowing what the numbers say and what to do about it from a creative standpoint

 - You have a proven track record of scaling social spend efficiently while maintaining or improving efficiency

 - You're not afraid to experiment and try new things, all while staying focused on driving incremental new customer revenue

 - You're a strong cross-functional collaborator who cares about fostering great relationships across teams

 - You thrive in a fast-paced, startup environment where priorities shift and speed matters

Need to Have

 - 5+ years of experience in paid social strategy and execution, with meaningful time at a high-growth DTC or e-commerce brand or performance agency

 - Deep, current hands-on fluency in Meta Ads Manager and TikTok Ads, including structured testing across bidding, creative, and audience

 - Strong understanding of performance metrics including ROAS, CAC, CPA, LTV, incrementality, and attribution — and the ability to validate what's actually driving performance before scaling

 - Comfortable with raw data and ad platform reporting; ability to extract clear next steps from complex data sets

 - Background managing creative for licensed partnerships or co-branded collaborations

 - Eagerness to learn, experiment, and grow

Nice to Have

 - Experience with Looker or Google Data Studio to build dashboards and automate reporting

 - Familiarity with AppLovin, Pinterest, Snap, and/or Reddit as paid channels

 - Familiarity with weekly or high-cadence product drop environments

jobs.title: Property Manager (Retail)
jobs.description:
POSITION OVERVIEW

The Property Manager provides first-class property management services for a third-party client.  Day-to day responsibilities include financial and operational management for a retail property, including client interaction, tenant and vendor relations, lease administration, budgeting, capital project oversight and supervisory responsibility.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Responsible for the coordination of all property management-related activities, including day-to-day building operations, accounts payable, accounts receivable, reporting, and client/tenant/vendor relations.
• Work closely with Construction, Leasing, Marketing, and Accounting Teams to ensure the “Stream Team” is providing the highest level of service to our clients.
• Ensure all Stream policies and best practices are implemented and followed.
• Understand and ensure compliance with the Management Agreement(s) and all Client policies and procedures.
• Conduct routine property inspections and associated follow-ups to prevent/identify/resolve problems and exposures.
• Prepare and adhere to operating and capital budgets and re-forecasts as well as annual expense recovery estimates and reconciliations.
• Coordinate all property-related contracts, services, repairs, and capital projects.
• Prepare, review, and submit the monthly/quarterly/annual financial and operational reports as per Client requirements. Prepare monthly expense variance comments for the client(s).
• Review and approve invoices/AP batches, and monthly rent edits. Review and ensure the accuracy of the General Ledger.
• Tenant lease review and set up in the designated accounting system.
• Adhere to Stream property management annual audit.
• Coordinate real estate tax review process for the portfolio/assignment.
• Process and oversee all TI applications for accounting submission and payment.
• Maintain personal contact with all vendors, tenants, and clients.
• Respond to and resolve after-hours emergency calls as needed.
• Supervisory responsibility for designated personnel.
• Review, approve, and submit team expense reports and PTO requests.
• Assist in the completion of annual performance reviews and regularly communicate performance to direct reports.

• 3+ years of Retail Commercial Property Management experience required.
• Bachelor’s Degree preferred
• CPM, RPA designation (or in progress) preferred
• Strong written and verbal communication skills; experience interacting with clients, vendors, teammates, and management
• Experience preparing annual budgets, ownership reports, and CAM reconciliations
• Previous experience using real estate software (Yardi or MRI, Kardin, AvidXchange, IMPAK, or similar programs)
• Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, and Teams
• Analytical
• Ability to multitask
• Attributes that align with Stream's core values of Smart, Honest, Nice, and Passionate

jobs.title: Shop Technician Apprentice
jobs.description:
At RES, we’re looking for purpose-driven individuals who are passionate about restoration and sustainability, and who want their work to make a lasting environmental impact. Our team members go above and beyond, bringing initiative, integrity, and a strong work ethic to every project. Collaboration is key—we thrive on teamwork, open communication, and diverse perspectives. In a field that constantly changes, we value those who are resilient, adaptable, and resourceful in the face of challenges. If you're intellectually curious, eager to learn, and ready to help restore ecosystems and protect natural resources, you’ll find your place here.

RES is a leader in ecological restoration and environmental solutions. Our field teams rely on trucks, heavy equipment, and specialized tools to deliver restoration work safely and effectively. The Shop Technician Apprenticeship Program is designed to build the next generation of RES shop and fleet talent through paid, hands-on learning, structured mentorship, and technical training.

About the Program

The Shop Technician Apprentice Program is a structured pathway for individuals who want to build a career maintaining and repairing trucks, construction equipment, and shop assets. Apprentices will work alongside experienced technicians while developing skills in safety, preventive maintenance, diagnostics, repair, documentation, and equipment support. The program is modeled on the U.S. Department of Labor Diesel Mechanic apprenticeship framework, which includes approximately 6,000 hours of on-the-job learning over about three years, supplemented by related technical instruction. Apprentices progress through defined learning stages and may receive wage progression as skills, hours, training, and performance milestones are achieved.

What You’ll Learn

As a Shop Technician Apprentice, you will develop hands-on experience in:

• Safe shop practices, PPE, equipment securement, and environmental procedures

• Preventive maintenance, including oil changes, lubrication, batteries, filters, and inspections

• Basic repair of trucks, trailers, construction equipment, and mechanical systems

• Brake systems, tires, steering components, guards, bolts, and safety devices

• Use of hand tools, power tools, diagnostic tools, gauges, and technical repair resources

• Diesel and gas engine systems, fuel systems, transmissions, gearboxes, and differentials

• Electrical systems, lights, circuits, emissions systems, and computer-controlled components

• Hydraulic systems, lifting equipment, pumps, compressors, and heavy equipment components

• Work order documentation, parts communication, and repair observations

What You’ll Do

• Assist experienced technicians with inspections, maintenance, repairs, and troubleshooting.

• Perform routine service tasks on trucks, construction equipment, and shop equipment.

• Learn to diagnose mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and equipment performance issues.

• Use technical manuals, repair platforms, and diagnostic tools to support repair decisions.

• Maintain a clean, organized, and safe shop environment.

• Communicate equipment issues, parts needs, repair status, and safety concerns to the shop manager or lead technician.

• Participate in required training, certifications, and program check-ins.

• Support field teams by helping keep RES equipment safe, functional, and ready for work.

Program Benefits

• Paid, hands-on training with experienced RES technicians.

• Structured learning pathway with clear expectations and progression milestones.

• Exposure to trucks, construction equipment, heavy equipment, and restoration-related fleet assets.

• Opportunity to pursue certifications and technical training.

• Career path toward Shop Technician I and future advancement in fleet, equipment, and operations roles.

Minimum Qualifications

• Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record.

• Ability to lift up to 50 lbs and work in a shop or outdoor environment.

• Interest in trucks, construction equipment, engines, tools, or mechanical systems.

• Ability to follow instructions, document work, and communicate clearly with team members.

• Willingness to participate in structured training and pursue certifications as needed.

Preferred Qualifications

• High school diploma or GED.

• Trade school, technical school, diesel, automotive, welding, heavy equipment, or shop experience.

• ASE, OSHA, forklift, CDL, or other relevant certification, or interest in pursuing certification.

• Prior experience with auto repair, farm equipment, construction equipment, small engines, or mechanical troubleshooting.

Please note that the “Day in the Life” section is not intended to be an exhaustive list of job duties, but rather a representative snapshot of typical responsibilities and work experiences at RES.

RES is an Equal Opportunity Employer and a VEVRAA Federal Contractor. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.description:
About the Company
 
At Flow, we’re reimagining what it means to live, work, and connect. More than just a real estate company, Flow is a brand, a technology platform, and an operations ecosystem spanning condominiums, hotels, multifamily residences, and office spaces. We’re building a new kind of living experience: one that’s flexible, connected, and designed to create genuine community and real value for the people who call Flow home.
 
Our mission is oneness:  prioritizing our residents and their experiences, and fostering connection with ourselves, their neighbors, and the natural world. By putting people at the center of everything we do, we’re creating vibrant, human-centered communities where life, work, creativity, and play all come together in one place.


About the Role 
Flow is seeking an experienced Lead IT Engineer — Properties & Hospitality to own the systems configuration, platform integration, and commissioning layer across its growing residential and hospitality portfolio. This role operates at the software and systems level — configuring platforms, integrating systems, validating performance, and ensuring every technology layer at a Flow property functions as intended.
This role works closely and continuously with the Sr. IT Field Technician — together they cover the full scope of property technology at Flow. While the Sr. IT Field Technician focuses on the physical layer (cabling, hardware installation, and low-voltage infrastructure), this role focuses on making those systems work: programming, configuration, integration, and ongoing platform support. The two roles are deeply interdependent and will be on-site together across deployments, troubleshooting, and new property buildouts. Both report directly to the Head of IT.
This is a senior individual contributor role requiring deep platform expertise, strong independent judgment, and the ability to manage multiple active projects across a growing property portfolio with minimal supervision.

jobs.title: Part-Time Group Therapist, Evening Program
jobs.description:
Weekly outpatient therapy isn't always enough, and a trip to the ER isn't the only answer. Patients and their families rely on Compass Health Center when in crisis – every day, we help people overcome depression, anxiety, suicidality, obsessions/compulsions, trauma, chronic pain, and other obstacles in order for our patients to live freely.

About This Role

At the core of Compass we believe in the power of community and connection, which is why we are committed to our group-based programming. As a group therapist, you will spend the majority of your time with our patients facilitating evidenced based groups using modalities like CBT, DBT, and ACT. We are seeking new and experienced clinicians with a passion for delivering dynamic and informative groups for our patients. If you are seeking an opportunity to provide exceptional care, we’d love to have you on our team.

Our centrally located Chicago office is nestled in the vibrant neighborhood of North Center, not to mention the social events hosted on our fully furnished rooftop!

This is a part-time position Monday through Friday with the specific schedule based on program needs. The scheduling will cover evening hours, between 12:00-8:00 PM CST.

What You'll Do:

• Developing and implementing DBT/CBT skill groups, working with ages 8-14 years old

• Providing crisis intervention and staff support, as needed

• Developing and documenting treatment plans and weekly update

• Co-facilitating creative expression and other experiential therapeutic groups

• Assisting program director in supporting families through phone coaching and follow-up calls

• Checking in with treatment team about changes and progress for individual patients

• Providing clinical observations and insights during interdisciplinary meetings

• Providing individual support to patients, as needed

• Providing support to other team members in various treatment groups

• Providing guidance and support for milieu staff during skills and executive functioning therapy activities/instruction

• Participating in discharge planning for patients

• Other duties, as assigned

Who You Are:

• Master’s in Social Work/Clinical Counseling or other relevant Master’s/Doctoral programs

• Hold or be eligible for one of the following licensures: LSW, LPC, LCSW, LCPC, MSW, AMFT, LMFT, PsyD, or PhD (preferred)

• 1 + year of post-Master’s clinical experience, or a relevant master’s level internship

• Possess a core skill set of Cognitive Behavior Therapy (CBT) and Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)

• Experience with patients in crisis, and a strong passion for working within high acuity environments

We are committed to a fair and equitable work environment. The expected compensation range for this role is below. This range includes multiple career path levels across the organization; where you fall in the range is dependent upon a number of factors including, but not limited to, your years of experience, type of experience, location, and education/certifications. Compass reserves the right to update these ranges.

Compensation

$47,000—$65,000 USD

We know job descriptions can be intimidating, so if this sounds like an opportunity for you, please don't hesitate to apply!

Who We Are

Compass Health Center is a recognized leader in crisis-level mental health, bringing passion, connection, and patient-centered care to the Partial Hospitalization and Intensive Outpatient space (PHP/IOP). Based in Chicagoland, we serve hundreds of patients every day, ranging from ages 5 through adulthood, in our onsite facilities or through our flourishing virtual programming. Compass fills a critical gap between outpatient and inpatient care through an intermediate level of Behavioral Healthcare.

A few more things we want you to know: our values are super important to us, and hopefully will be to you, too. Cultural humility, teamwork, continuous improvement, connection, patient centered care, passion, innovation, and agility should be your power sources. Joining Compass is an opportunity to feel fulfilled through a joint mission towards healing our communities.

Benefits & Perks

We know that you will be dedicated to your purpose here. We look at that investment as a two-way street. We are proud to offer plenty of space for growth, and opportunities to pursue continuous development within our organization.

For eligible positions, our other benefits include: comprehensive medical/dental/vision plans, 401k program with company matching, generous PTO (including competitive parental leave after 1 year of employment), and continuous training through CEU seminars and volunteering opportunities.

What’s Next?

Compass is committed to cultivating diverse and dynamic teams who exude passion for their craft, so whether or not you check all the boxes, we encourage you to apply – we’d be grateful to hear from you!

jobs.title: Packaging Production Worker General Labor 1st Shift

Packaging Production Worker General Labor

SHIFT: Monday-Thursday,  6:00 a.m.- 4:30 p.m.

The role of the Production Worker is to perform necessary functions in order to efficiently, safely, and correctly prepare and process raw material to prepare it for cooking or cut & package finished product in preparation for shipment to customer.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The duties and responsibilities of this position shall consist of, but not be limited to, the following:

General:

• Follow daily production schedule and achieve specified goals.
• Ensure product conforms to specifications.
• Prevent and minimize rework and/or inedible.
• May require working on taping machines, shrink wrap machines, pallet jacks, trash and recycling compactors.
• Perform standard operating procedures of production and inspection functions as directed.
• Successfully complete all necessary technical training and skills verification as directed.
• Successfully complete all necessary soft skills training as directed.
• Return from breaks in a timely manner; notify lead/foreman/supervisor before leaving the department.
• Accurately complete all necessary paperwork as directed.
• Attend all department and company scheduled meetings.
• Works scheduled shift as assigned.
• Maintain a safe, clean and organized work area.
• Immediately report all accidents and deficiencies to the lead/foreman/supervisor.
• Ensure safety devices are installed and working properly.
• Suggest improvements; continuously improve the quality of all support activities.
• Perform all required duties within OSHA and company safety standards.
• Follows set company and OSHA safety rules, regulations, and guidelines at all times.
• Follow Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs), Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) training, along with company pre-requisite programs, Standard Operating Procedures (SOP’s), and Standard Sanitation Operating Procedures (SSOP’s).
• Performs other duties and responsibilities as necessary.
• Ensure products are correctly labeled and identified for proper disposition.
• Keep record of products used to follow FIFO (first in – first out).

Ready to Eat:

• Count and place packages in appropriate caddies, maintaining accurate records, washing and sanitizing carts, racks, and trucks.
• Handling finished product, placing it continuously in trays or assembly lines to be shipped to our customers.
• Making pallets by stacking boxes onto pallets, preparing the pallet with cardboard wrapping, manually shrink wrapping, and pulling/pushing pallets with manual pallet jack.

REQUIRED EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Required Education: None

Required Experience: None

Preferred: Knowledge of warehouse and assembly line experience is a plus.

• Must be able to work in a fast-paced environment.

• Must be able to communicate with co-workers and supervisor.

jobs.title: Trade Surveillance Analyst 1 — Financial Crimes Department
jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Alpaca is a US-headquartered self-clearing broker-dealer and brokerage infrastructure for stocks, ETFs, options, crypto, fixed income, 24/5 trading, and more. Our recent Series D funding round brought our total investment to over $320 million, fueling our ambitious vision.

Amongst our subsidiaries, Alpaca is a licensed financial services company, serving hundreds of financial institutions across 40 countries with our institutional-grade APIs. This includes broker-dealers, investment advisors, wealth managers, hedge funds, and crypto exchanges, totalling over 9 million brokerage accounts.

Our global team is a diverse group of experienced engineers, traders, and brokerage professionals who are working to achieve our mission of opening financial services to everyone on the planet. We're deeply committed to open-source contributions and fostering a vibrant community, continuously enhancing our award-winning, developer-friendly API and the robust infrastructure behind it.

Alpaca is proudly backed by top-tier global investors, including Portage Ventures, Spark Capital, Tribe Capital, Social Leverage, Horizons Ventures, Unbound, SBI Group, Derayah Financial, Elefund, and Y Combinator.

Our Team Members:

We're a dynamic team of 380+ globally distributed members who thrive working from our favorite places around the world, with teammates spanning the USA, Canada, Japan, Hungary, Nigeria, Brazil, the UK, and beyond!

We're searching for passionate individuals eager to contribute to Alpaca's rapid growth. If you align with our core values—Stay Curious, Have Empathy, and Be Accountable—and are ready to make a significant impact, we encourage you to apply.

Your Role:

Join Alpaca Securities’ dynamic and fully remote Compliance team dedicated to safeguarding the integrity of the financial markets. In this role, you will play a critical part in supporting the firm’s BSA/AML, Anti-Fraud, and Securities Fraud Monitoring programs.  You will lead and support investigations, ensure adherence to regulatory requirements, and help build a scalable and risk-based compliance infrastructure that meets evolving business and regulatory demands.  This position reports directly to the AMLCO (Anti-Money Laundering Compliance Officer).

Key Responsibilities:

• Collaborate with the AMLCO to implement and refine investigative procedures cross CIP/KYC, AML, Anti-Fraud, and Securities Fraud Monitoring initiatives.

• Conduct in-depth investigations into potentially suspicious activity, including securities fraud, account manipulation, and other financial crimes identified through transaction monitoring alerts, escalations, and referrals.

• Prepare, document, and file Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) in compliance with

• FinCEN requirements and internal policies.

• Review and respond to sanctions screening alerts, FinCEN 314(a) and 314(b) requests, and other regulatory inquiries.

• Maintain and continuously update firm-wide risk assessments covering BSA/AML, sanctions, fraud, and securities surveillance programs.

jobs.title: Conventional Safety and Certification Lead
jobs.description:
Who We Are (video)

At JRC, we tackle some of the toughest challenges faced by the Department of Defense (DoD) and other government agencies. Our expertise in engineering innovation and semiconductor technologies allows us to deliver mission-critical microelectronics solutions, aerospace systems engineering, and cutting-edge research and development. By joining JRC, you’ll be part of a team that supports strategic deterrence and defense missions, playing a crucial role in ensuring the safety and security of the United States and its allies.

The Conventional Safety & Certification lead (SP04732) for the Limited Operational Capability (LOC) branch (SP047) is responsible for planning and managing conventional safety requirements, overseeing implementation, ensuring verification, and supporting certification for the LOC missile.  This position is responsible for managing the implementation of DoD Instruction 5000.69, DoD Joint Services Weapon and Laser System Safety Review Processes, at the flight-system and missile level to implement system safety review procedures and process when performing weapon system safety reviews.  This position is responsible for implementing policies and procedures to achieve LOC missile safety certifications for missile processing and handling ashore and deployment afloat.

• Serve as the principal engineer to assess system, missile, and ordnance safety policy and flow down implementable and verifiable missile requirements

• Lead oversight and approval of contractor safety feature implementation into missile and missile support equipment designs

• Represents LOC missile equities at Command-level safety meetings and forums

• Work collaboratively with external partners to assess, support, and document safety features and compliance within the baseline missile design(s)

• Advise as a safety expert and remain abreast of safety program changes and potential impacts to the LOC missile

• Support safety certification activities to proof, exercise, and assess readiness for safety certification

• Support safety certification activities that involve missile and flight-system equities

• Identify and mitigate technical risks across the system development and deployed lifecycle.

• Prepare material, support preparations, and provide technical advice during safety reviews and certification activities

• Work collaboratively with Weapon Integration Systems Engineering (WISE) team to achieve NOSSA and WSSERB safety certifications

🧠What You Bring to the Table

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering (Mechanical, Aerospace, Electrical, Systems, or related discipline).

• Minimum 5 years of experience in defense system engineering on an MDAP.

• Extensive knowledge of DoD Manual 5000.69, DoD Joint Services Weapon System Safety Review Process

• Knowledge of MIL-STD-882E, Standard Practice for System Safety

• Knowledge of Joint Services Software Safety Authorities (JS‐SSA) Software System Safety Implementation Process and Tasks supporting MIL‐STD‐882E

• Knowledge of the DoD 5000-series acquisition policies, including DoDI 5000.88 and 5000.02.

• Demonstrated experience in missile systems design, integration, and verification.

• Strong communication skills and ability to interface with OSD, Service PEOs, and FFRDC stakeholders.

• Active or recently adjudicated Top Secret clearance.

⭐Bonus Points

• Master’s degree in Systems Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or related field.

• DAWIA Advanced Certification in Engineering or Program Management.

• INCOSE CSEP/ESEP certification.

• Experience supporting nuclear-capable or strategic missile programs.

Additional Information:

This position requires regular interaction with senior DoW, FFRDC, and industry leadership. Travel (~ 50%) to test ranges, contractor facilities, weapons facilities, and government labs is required to support technical and programmatic reviews, integration events, and milestone readiness assessments.

• A collaborative work environment where teamwork, creativity, and innovation thrive

jobs.title: Principal Product Designer
jobs.description:
You'll be designing for people whose work actually matters: maintenance engineers, field service technicians, operations planners working in environments where the software either helps or gets in the way. The stakes are real and the problems are hard, which is exactly what makes this role interesting.

At IFS, product design means owning the full problem, not just the screens. You'll work in a cross-functional squad alongside engineers and product managers, with the scope and support to do the work properly. From problem framing through to something shipped and measured.

But the deeper question is harder than that. The industries IFS serves (field service, asset management, manufacturing, supply chain) are changing faster than the software that runs them. By 2030, we're not confident the interface paradigms we rely on today will still be the right ones. AI, ambient computing, voice, autonomous systems: any of these could fundamentally change how an operations planner or a field engineer interacts with software, or whether they interact with it at all.

That's not a problem we've solved. It's the problem you'd be working on.

What you'll do

Product Design

• Own design for defined feature areas end-to-end — from problem framing through to production-ready Figma files, with a clear rationale for every decision

• Work in a cross-functional squad with engineers and PMs, making real decisions rather than executing on someone else's brief

• Present design thinking to stakeholders with confidence — handling pushback with evidence, not just conviction

Discovery & Research

• Plan and run user interviews, JTBD analysis, and journey mapping independently — turning findings into clear design direction, not just a readout

• Track quantitative signals alongside qualitative insight, and use both to drive iteration

AI & Emerging Technology

• Design AI-driven features with a clear understanding of where AI helps and where it introduces risk — prompts, fallbacks, and human-in-the-loop moments included

• Bring a genuine perspective on how the interfaces we're building today might become obsolete — and what should replace them

Design Systems & Quality

• Contribute to the IFS design system by proposing reusable components and patterns rather than designing one-offs

• Apply WCAG 2.1+ accessibility standards from the start, and design for edge cases, error states, and real-world data — not just the happy path

You'll know it's working when your work ships, holds up in the field, and raises the bar for the next thing. Concretely: task success rates improve, UX-related support tickets drop, and the squad reaches for your work as a reference rather than a starting point.

You may be a good fit if you:

• You have at least three years of end-to-end product design experience — from discovery through to shipped product — and you can point to work that reflects real ownership, not just execution

• You're comfortable running your own research: planning the study, conducting interviews, synthesising findings, and turning them into a clear design direction

• You know how to work in a cross-functional squad — making real decisions alongside engineers and PMs, not waiting to be handed a brief

• You know Figma well and have the visual craft to back your thinking up

• You treat accessibility as a design constraint from the start, not a checklist at the end

• You've thought seriously about what AI means for the interfaces you build — not just as a feature to add, but as something that changes the fundamental design problem

• You measure your work — task success rates, support ticket volume, adoption — and use those signals to drive the next iteration

Strong candidates may also have:

• Experience shipping AI-driven features — prompts, fallbacks, human-in-the-loop moments — not just awareness of the concepts

• Familiarity with design tokens, contribution models, and what it means to design for a system rather than a screen

• Some exposure to quantitative signals: task success rates, funnel data, or A/B results — and a habit of using them

• Flexible paid time off, including sick and holiday
• Medical, dental, & vision insurance
• 401K with Company contribution
• Flexible spending accounts
• Life insurance and disability benefits
• Tuition assistance
• Community involvement and volunteering events

We embrace flexibility and hybrid work opportunities to support diverse needs and lifestyles, while also valuing inclusive workplace experiences. By fostering a sense of community, we drive innovation, strengthen connections, and nurture belonging. Our commitment ensures you can work in a way that suits you best, while also engaging with colleagues to share ideas and build meaningful relationships.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran. VEVRAA Federal Contractor, Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.title: Buyer/Purchaser
jobs.description:
Location: Onsite — Austin, TX

Employment Type: Direct Hire, Full Time

Job Title: Buyer/Purchaser



About 9 Mothers

The modern battlefield has changed. Cheap, autonomous suicide drones have turned the tactical advantage upside down, and the world is looking for a solution. At 9 Mothers, we aren’t just "innovating"—we are building the shield.

Backed by top-tier investors, we develop AI powered machines designed to intercept and neutralize Group 1/sUAS threats in real-time. Our flagship product is a low-power, counter-drone system built for the edge—on vehicles, at bases, or in a soldier's pack.



Why 9 Mothers?

While others build for "awareness" or "long-term research," we build for the immediate survival of those in harm’s way. We are a team of hackers, engineers, and mission-driven builders who value field-ready capability over polished slide decks. If you want to see your code or hardware in the field next month—not next year—this is your playground.



Position Summary

9 Mothers builds counter-UAS systems — robotic shotgun turret platforms and a proprietary belt-fed shotgun system. Everything we ship starts with parts: custom electronics, machined metal, actuators, cables, and cameras, sourced from vendors we trust. Today, engineers buy their own parts. That stops working the moment we move from prototype and small-run quantities into production — which is exactly where we are headed over the next 12 months.

You will be our first dedicated buyer and, initially, a department of one. You will own procurement end to end: finding parts, qualifying vendors, negotiating, placing and chasing POs, and building the purchasing processes and systems this company will scale on. As we grow into production, this role grows with the company — the person who defines purchasing here has a clear path to leading the function.

Two things make this role harder than a typical buyer seat. First, we run on scarce, allocated electronics — NVIDIA Jetson modules, cameras, specialty sensors — and you need to be the person who can find them when distributors say twelve months. Second, we are a defense company: our supply base must exclude Chinese vendors, with a strong preference for US suppliers, and you own keeping it that way.



Essential Duties

Sourcing & Procurement (Primary)

 - Source and purchase the full robotics bill of materials: custom electronics and PCB assemblies, CNC-machined metal parts, actuators and motors, cable assemblies, cameras and sensors, and supporting COTS hardware

 - Hunt down hard-to-find and allocated electronics — NVIDIA Jetson modules, GPUs, image sensors — through authorized distribution, direct manufacturer relationships, and carefully vetted secondary-market channels, managing counterfeit risk and allocation constraints

 - Run the quote-to-PO cycle: solicit and compare quotes, negotiate pricing, payment terms, and lead times, place purchase orders, and track and expedite deliveries against build schedules

 - Own vendor selection within our trade-compliance constraints: build and maintain a non-Chinese supply base with a strong preference for US vendors, verifying country of origin down to the component level where required

Building the Purchasing Function

 - Define the company's purchasing processes from scratch: PO workflow and approvals, vendor onboarding and qualification, receiving and inspection handoff, and spend tracking

 - Select and stand up purchasing tooling — from spreadsheets that actually work today to an ERP/MRP system that supports production volumes

 - Build and maintain the approved vendor list; work with engineering on part numbering, BOM hygiene, and approved alternates

 - Give the company visibility: report on spend, open orders, lead-time risk, and cost trends so engineering and leadership can plan around reality

Scaling to Production

 - Transition the supply base from prototype and small-run buys to production purchasing: qualify vendors for volume, establish second sources for critical parts, and negotiate volume pricing, blanket orders, and scheduled releases

 - Plan procurement against production build schedules — long-lead items ordered early, safety stock on allocation-risk parts, and no line-down surprises

 - Work with engineering on BOM health for production: component lifecycle and end-of-life monitoring, alternate qualification, and cost-down opportunities as volumes grow

Compliance & Risk

 - Procure within ITAR constraints and maintain the documentation to prove it: country-of-origin records, vendor certifications, and traceability appropriate for defense customers

 - Screen the supply chain against prohibited-source requirements (e.g., NDAA Section 889 covered entities) and keep Chinese-origin content out of the product

 - Protect against counterfeit components — buy through authorized channels by default, and apply rigorous vetting (testing, escrow, documentation) when the secondary market is the only option



Required Qualifications

 - 5+ years of procurement/purchasing experience for physical hardware products — robotics, defense, aerospace, automotive, industrial equipment, or similar electromechanical systems

 - Proven ability to source scarce and allocated electronics: you have found parts others couldn't (GPU modules, embedded compute, image sensors, or similar), and you know the authorized-distribution landscape, the broker market, and how to avoid counterfeits

 - Experience buying across our categories: custom PCB assemblies, machined metal parts, actuators/motors, cable assemblies, and cameras or sensors

 - Experience supporting a product transition from prototype/low-volume to production purchasing — vendor qualification, volume negotiation, and lead-time planning

 - Track record of building or substantially defining purchasing processes, not just executing within an established system

 - Self-sufficient as a department of one: you set your own priorities, close your own loops, and don't need a manager to unblock you

 - Strong negotiator with vendors of all sizes — from Fortune 500 distributors to two-person machine shops

 - US person (citizen or lawful permanent resident) — required for ITAR compliance



Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience in a defense or ITAR-regulated environment; working familiarity with NDAA Section 889, country-of-origin verification, and government customer flow-downs

 - Experience selecting or implementing an ERP/MRP system at a growing hardware company

 - Existing relationships with electronics distributors (Arrow, Avnet, Digi-Key, Mouser, etc.), embedded-compute vendors, and domestic machine shops or contract manufacturers

 - Experience with formal supplier qualification, supplier audits, or purchasing in an AS9100/ISO 9001 environment

 - Early-stage startup experience — comfortable with ambiguity, thin process, and building the airplane while flying it



What Success Looks Like

In the first 90 days, purchasing runs through you and nobody misses the old way: engineers hand you a part number or a drawing and parts show up on time. You own the vendor relationships that matter, you've found at least one "impossible" part, and a real PO process exists where none did before.

On an ongoing basis, builds don't slip because of parts. Long-lead and allocation-risk items are ordered before they become emergencies, costs come down as volumes go up, and the supply base is production-ready, second-sourced where it counts, and clean of prohibited vendors. When we scale, purchasing is a reason we can — not a reason we can't.



About the Interview

 1. Application screening phone call (30 min)

 2. Virtual interview with the Director of Hardware Operations (45 min via MS Teams)

 3. Onsite interview + meet the team

 4. Offer



Work Environment

This role is based on-site in Austin, TX at our shop, alongside the engineering and manufacturing team. The environment is a working R&D and manufacturing facility for weapons systems — expect an active shop floor and proximity to live-fire test activity, with strict adherence to safety protocols. Occasional travel for vendor visits, supplier audits, and industry events.

jobs.description:
Ingram Content Group (ICG) is currently seeking a Sr Systems Engineer to join our team in LaVergne, TN (Greater Nashville area).  This Senior Systems Engineer is responsible for the administration, security, and optimization of the organization's enterprise Microsoft 365 environment, with primary ownership of SharePoint Online, OneDrive for Business, Microsoft Teams, and Exchange Online. Serves as the senior technical authority for the Microsoft 365 platform, partnering with the Security & Compliance team on data governance, access controls, and Microsoft Purview initiatives, and supporting automation and AI-readiness efforts involving Power Automate and Microsoft Copilot. Acts as the escalation point for complex issues referred by the Service Desk and End User Support teams and is expected to operate with a high degree of independence and sound judgment. This position will be expected by hybrid and work from the Ingram headquarters 4 days per week.

Want to help explore and build new ways to deliver content to the world?

At Ingram, our Technology team is blazing a trail by providing content distribution services to thousands of publishers with key initiatives around business intelligence, machine learning, continuous integration and omnichannel.  We support diverse people and technology that highlights innovation through SaaS platforms, metadata, cloud, and containerization.   Our teams are agile, and emphasize authenticity, creativity, and transparency upon a fact-based foundation.

The world is reading, and it is our goal to connect as many people as possible to the content they want in the simplest ways.  If you are an IT professional who strives to deliver results through collaborative partnerships, understanding what drives business, and enjoys working in a connected culture, we can’t wait to meet you!

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering or a related field, or directly related year-for-year experience.
• 5 years of systems engineering or related experience, including progressive experience administering Microsoft 365 at the enterprise level, including SharePoint Online, OneDrive, Microsoft Teams, and Exchange Online.

We have a preference for:

• Deep working knowledge of Microsoft 365 administration, including tenant-level configuration and cross-service dependencies.
• Strong understanding of SharePoint Online architecture, permissions models, hub sites, and site provisioning at enterprise scale.
• Proficiency administering Microsoft Teams policies, voice/calling features, and Teams governance.
• Solid understanding of Exchange Online mail flow, mail hygiene, and message security controls.
• Working knowledge of Microsoft Purview capabilities, including DLP, retention policies, sensitivity labels, and eDiscovery.
• Familiarity with Microsoft Copilot licensing, data readiness requirements, and adoption/pilot considerations.
• Hands-on experience building and maintaining workflows and automations using Power Automate.

• Manages Exchange Online mail flow, transport rules, distribution groups, shared mailboxes, and mailbox permissions.
• Serves as the Tier 3 escalation point for complex M365 issues referred by the Service Desk and End User Support teams.

• Designs and maintains automated workflows using Power Automate to streamline provisioning, approvals, and other administrative processes.
• Supports Microsoft Copilot readiness activities, including permissions hygiene reviews, license planning, and pilot rollout support.
• Manages Microsoft 365 license allocation, usage reporting, and cost optimization across the tenant.
• Creates and maintains technical documentation, standard operating procedures, and knowledge
• base articles for administered services.
• Monitors the Microsoft 365 Message Center and roadmap changes and assess and communicates the enterprise impact of upcoming feature changes.
• Participates in incident response and root cause analysis for Microsoft 365 service disruptions.
• Provide technical mentorship and guidance to junior administrators and Service Desk staff on Microsoft 365-related issues.

jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Virtuous is on a mission to inspire global generosity by helping nonprofits build better relationships with their donors. We offer a modern software platform that provides mid-sized charities with elegant tools for fundraising, marketing, volunteerism, and online giving.



Our talented team is driven to disrupt the status quo in the nonprofit sector. We are hungry, humble, and committed to delivering best-in-class software solutions, customer success interactions, and sales experiences to the world’s leading nonprofits 

 

We also recognize the importance of giving back and making a difference in the communities where we live and work. That's why we practice radical generosity by volunteering at nonprofits or going the extra mile for our team and the customers we serve. We take our work seriously, but we don’t take ourselves too seriously. We believe that life is too short not to love what you do. 



The ideal candidate for Virtuous embodies our values by:

 - Asking questions with a spirit of curiosity

 - Giving feedback freely with candor & grace, welcoming it in return

 - Displaying a passion for philanthropy and technology 

 - Serving with joy. Everyone is willing to make the coffee!

 - Celebrating the wins & milestones of others 

 - Assuming good intent & demonstrating trust in others 

 - Pursuing relationships with people different from themselves & creates space to be human
   
   

Find our core values & more here https://virtuous.org/company/about/.




POSITION SUMMARY

You’ll be responsible for a named account list of nonprofit organizations we seek to partner with. You’ll spend your days engaging with multiple departments within target organizations to generate pipeline, facilitate qualifying calls and conduct ROI evaluations with key decision makers, and execute a seamless handoff of qualified accounts to Account Executives.



In addition to daily account development and fielding inbound leads, you’ll partner with marketing and sales to design and execute individualized outreach emails and plays that engage your assigned accounts. 



Nonprofit Sales Development Reps are a critical part of our growth plan and essential as we rapidly increase the number of nonprofits we serve. You’ll report to the NDR Manager and focus on three primary areas to generate pipeline: target account research, outbound account development and engagement, and inbound account qualification and booking.




RESPONSIBILITIES

Account Development — 85%

 - Fielding inbound sales leads including demo requests, in-market intent leads, and brand event leads

 - Using multiple channels and tactics to maintain a high volume of outbound outreach activities each day to multiple stakeholders within assigned nonprofit organizations

 - Using strategy and creativity to reach key decision makers within provided target accounts

 - Facilitating qualifying calls and conducting ROI evaluations with high-level key decision makers

Company: Loenbro, LLC
Business Unit/Department:
Location: Gilbert, Arizona

Reports to: Pre-Construction Director

Employment Type: Full Time
FLSA Classification: Exempt

About Loenbro

Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.

At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation.

Job Summary

The Chief Estimator will be responsible for leading a team in providing full electrical estimating and proposal preparation for all types of industrial facilities, including both new construction and maintenance, for projects up to $20M in value. Estimates will cover all types of contracts in the energy, mining, power, manufacturing, pulp/paper, agricultural, pharma, and other industries which Loenbro serves.

Essential Job Responsibilities

• Leading and managing entire estimating team for specific project or region.

• Coordinate attendance to bid meetings and walk through various client locations to determine project scope, complexities, accessibilities, and required content of proposal.

• Review instructions and proposal specifications, drawings, technical data necessary to provide a complete proposal for the customer.

• Review and incorporate historical data from purchase orders, subcontracts, previous proposals, job reports, etc. into unit and man hour figures for cost and production-based estimates.

• Prepare full-scope estimates on small, medium, and large-scale projects, in a timely and accurate manner.

jobs.title: Buyer/Purchaser, Senior
jobs.description:
Location: Onsite — Austin, TX

Employment Type: Direct Hire, Full Time

Job Title: Senior Buyer/Purchaser

 

About 9 Mothers

The modern battlefield has changed. Cheap, autonomous suicide drones have turned the tactical advantage upside down, and the world is looking for a solution. At 9 Mothers, we aren’t just "innovating"—we are building the shield.

Backed by top-tier investors, we develop AI powered machines designed to intercept and neutralize Group 1/sUAS threats in real-time. Our flagship product is a low-power, counter-drone system built for the edge—on vehicles, at bases, or in a soldier's pack.

 

Why 9 Mothers?

While others build for "awareness" or "long-term research," we build for the immediate survival of those in harm’s way. We are a team of hackers, engineers, and mission-driven builders who value field-ready capability over polished slide decks. If you want to see your code or hardware in the field next month—not next year—this is your playground.

 

Position Summary

9 Mothers builds counter-UAS systems — robotic shotgun turret platforms and a proprietary belt-fed shotgun system. Everything we ship starts with parts: custom electronics, machined metal, actuators, cables, and cameras, sourced from vendors we trust. Today, engineers buy their own parts. That stops working the moment we move from prototype and small-run quantities into production — which is exactly where we are headed over the next 12 months.

You will be our first dedicated buyer and, initially, a department of one. You will own procurement end to end: finding parts, qualifying vendors, negotiating, placing and chasing POs, and building the purchasing processes and systems this company will scale on. As we grow into production, this role grows with the company — the person who defines purchasing here has a clear path to leading the function.

Two things make this role harder than a typical buyer seat. First, we run on scarce, allocated electronics — NVIDIA Jetson modules, cameras, specialty sensors — and you need to be the person who can find them when distributors say twelve months. Second, we are a defense company: our supply base must exclude Chinese vendors, with a strong preference for US suppliers, and you own keeping it that way.

 

Essential Duties

Sourcing & Procurement (Primary)

 - Source and purchase the full robotics bill of materials: custom electronics and PCB assemblies, CNC-machined metal parts, actuators and motors, cable assemblies, cameras and sensors, and supporting COTS hardware

 - Hunt down hard-to-find and allocated electronics — NVIDIA Jetson modules, GPUs, image sensors — through authorized distribution, direct manufacturer relationships, and carefully vetted secondary-market channels, managing counterfeit risk and allocation constraints

 - Run the quote-to-PO cycle: solicit and compare quotes, negotiate pricing, payment terms, and lead times, place purchase orders, and track and expedite deliveries against build schedules

 - Own vendor selection within our trade-compliance constraints: build and maintain a non-Chinese supply base with a strong preference for US vendors, verifying country of origin down to the component level where required

Building the Purchasing Function

 - Define the company's purchasing processes from scratch: PO workflow and approvals, vendor onboarding and qualification, receiving and inspection handoff, and spend tracking

 - Select and stand up purchasing tooling — from spreadsheets that actually work today to an ERP/MRP system that supports production volumes

 - Build and maintain the approved vendor list; work with engineering on part numbering, BOM hygiene, and approved alternates

 - Give the company visibility: report on spend, open orders, lead-time risk, and cost trends so engineering and leadership can plan around reality

Scaling to Production

 - Transition the supply base from prototype and small-run buys to production purchasing: qualify vendors for volume, establish second sources for critical parts, and negotiate volume pricing, blanket orders, and scheduled releases

 - Plan procurement against production build schedules — long-lead items ordered early, safety stock on allocation-risk parts, and no line-down surprises

 - Work with engineering on BOM health for production: component lifecycle and end-of-life monitoring, alternate qualification, and cost-down opportunities as volumes grow

Compliance & Risk

 - Procure within ITAR constraints and maintain the documentation to prove it: country-of-origin records, vendor certifications, and traceability appropriate for defense customers

 - Screen the supply chain against prohibited-source requirements (e.g., NDAA Section 889 covered entities) and keep Chinese-origin content out of the product

 - Protect against counterfeit components — buy through authorized channels by default, and apply rigorous vetting (testing, escrow, documentation) when the secondary market is the only option

 

Required Qualifications

 - 7+ years of procurement/purchasing experience for physical hardware products — robotics, defense, aerospace, automotive, industrial equipment, or similar electromechanical systems

 - Proven ability to source scarce and allocated electronics: you have found parts others couldn't (GPU modules, embedded compute, image sensors, or similar), and you know the authorized-distribution landscape, the broker market, and how to avoid counterfeits

 - Experience buying across our categories: custom PCB assemblies, machined metal parts, actuators/motors, cable assemblies, and cameras or sensors

 - Experience supporting a product transition from prototype/low-volume to production purchasing — vendor qualification, volume negotiation, and lead-time planning

 - Track record of building or substantially defining purchasing processes, not just executing within an established system

 - Self-sufficient as a department of one: you set your own priorities, close your own loops, and don't need a manager to unblock you

 - Strong negotiator with vendors of all sizes — from Fortune 500 distributors to two-person machine shops

 - US person (citizen or lawful permanent resident) — required for ITAR compliance

 

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience in a defense or ITAR-regulated environment; working familiarity with NDAA Section 889, country-of-origin verification, and government customer flow-downs

 - Experience selecting or implementing an ERP/MRP system at a growing hardware company

 - Existing relationships with electronics distributors (Arrow, Avnet, Digi-Key, Mouser, etc.), embedded-compute vendors, and domestic machine shops or contract manufacturers

 - Experience with formal supplier qualification, supplier audits, or purchasing in an AS9100/ISO 9001 environment

 - Early-stage startup experience — comfortable with ambiguity, thin process, and building the airplane while flying it

 

What Success Looks Like

In the first 90 days, purchasing runs through you and nobody misses the old way: engineers hand you a part number or a drawing and parts show up on time. You own the vendor relationships that matter, you've found at least one "impossible" part, and a real PO process exists where none did before.

On an ongoing basis, builds don't slip because of parts. Long-lead and allocation-risk items are ordered before they become emergencies, costs come down as volumes go up, and the supply base is production-ready, second-sourced where it counts, and clean of prohibited vendors. When we scale, purchasing is a reason we can — not a reason we can't.

 

About the Interview

 1. Application screening phone call (30 min)

 2. Virtual interview with the Director of Hardware Operations (45 min via MS Teams)

 3. Onsite interview + meet the team

 4. Offer

 

Work Environment

This role is based on-site in Austin, TX at our shop, alongside the engineering and manufacturing team. The environment is a working R&D and manufacturing facility for weapons systems — expect an active shop floor and proximity to live-fire test activity, with strict adherence to safety protocols. Occasional travel for vendor visits, supplier audits, and industry events.

jobs.title: AI Voice Experience Designer

About Dialpad
Dialpad is the AI platform for customer experience, built to resolve customer problems in real time across voice and digital. Our AI agents learn from your best human agents and improve with every interaction, helping organizations understand their customers, deliver better experiences, increase operational efficiencies, and build a lasting competitive advantage.

Unlike legacy systems built to route and answer, or standalone agentic bot vendors built to deflect, Dialpad was built to resolve. Our AI agents and human agents operate on a single platform with shared context, allowing Agentic AI to resolve issues, advance deals, and eliminate busywork through automation while seamlessly handing conversations to humans when needed, with full context preserved.

Market-leading brands, including Randstad, Motorola Solutions, Netflix, the San Diego Padres, the Colorado Rockies Baseball Club, and Cal Athletics, trust Dialpad. Dialpad is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, GV, ICONIQ Capital, and T-Mobile.

Being a Dialer
At Dialpad, AI isn’t just a feature; it’s how our teams do their best work every day. We put powerful AI tools in every employee’s hands so they can move faster, think bigger, and achieve more.

We believe every conversation matters. And we’ve built the platform that turns those conversations into insight and action, for our customers and ourselves.

We look for people who are intensely curious and hold themselves to a high bar. Our ambition is significant, and achieving it requires a team that operates at the highest level. We seek individuals who embody our core traits: Scrappy, Curious, Optimistic, Persistent, and Empathetic.

Your role
As an AI Voice Experience Designer, you'll embed with our most strategic Agentic AI Early Access customers to help bring their AI agents into production. You'll own the end-to-end customer experience—shaping how an AI agent sounds, behaves, and performs until it consistently resolves real customer conversations.

You'll work closely with Professional Services, Product, Engineering, and our Agent Experience Design team to tune agent behavior, refine voice and personality, improve conversational fluency, and deliver measurable business outcomes. Beyond individual customer deployments, you'll help identify patterns that improve the product for every future customer.

This position reports to our Professional Services organization and is a remote, customer-facing role requiring travel as needed.

What you'll do

• Own the end-to-end AI agent experience for assigned Early Access Program (EAP) customers, from implementation through production readiness.

• Partner directly with customers to understand their business, workflows, and success criteria, translating those needs into agent behavior.

• Configure and tune AI agents by selecting voices, refining personas, optimizing prompts, and improving conversational performance.

• Continuously improve agent fluency through pronunciation tuning, text normalization, domain-specific language optimization, and conversational refinement.

• Drive customer deployments to defined quality standards, including consistency, fluency, latency (CFL), resolution rates, and containment targets.

• Analyze live conversations, identify opportunities for improvement, and rapidly iterate agent behavior based on customer feedback and production performance.

• Collaborate closely with Product, Engineering, and Agent Experience Design teams to surface learnings that improve the platform for all customers.

• Serve as a trusted advisor throughout the customer journey, ensuring customers are confident deploying AI agents into production.

Skills you'll bring

• Experience leading customer-facing implementations, deployments, or solution delivery for complex technical products.

• Strong understanding of conversational AI, large language models (LLMs), prompt engineering, or AI agent behavior.

• Experience working with text-to-speech (TTS), conversational design, voice interfaces, or natural language processing is highly desirable.

• Excellent written communication skills with the ability to craft natural, consistent AI personalities and conversational experiences.

• Strong customer consulting and relationship management skills, with the ability to navigate ambiguity and build trust with executive stakeholders.

• Analytical mindset with experience using metrics and customer feedback to improve product outcomes.

• Comfortable working in fast-paced, early-stage environments where rapid iteration and experimentation are expected.

• Willingness to travel to customer sites as needed.

• Experience supporting customers in regulated or high-complexity industries such as healthcare, financial services, or legal is a plus.

Why Join Dialpad

• Work at the center of the AI transformation in business communications

• Build and ship agentic AI products that are redefining how companies operate

• Join a team where AI amplifies every employee’s impact

• Competitive salary, comprehensive benefits, and real opportunities for growth

We believe in investing in our people. Dialpad offers competitive benefits and perks, cutting-edge AI tools, and a robust training program that help you reach your full potential. We have designed our offices to be inclusive, offering a vibrant environment to cultivate collaboration and connection. Our exceptional culture, repeatedly recognized as a Great Place to Work, ensures that every employee feels valued and empowered to contribute to our collective success.

Don’t meet every single requirement? If you’re excited about this role and possess the fundamental traits, drive, and strong ambition we seek, but your experience doesn’t meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply.

Dialpad is an equal-opportunity employer. We are dedicated to creating a community of inclusion and an environment free from discrimination or harassment.

Realizar a devida diligência através da verificação e confirmação das instruções comerciais e da documentação de apoio relacionada, em conformidade com os regulamentos, decisões e normas comerciais, de modo a garantir o cumprimento da regulamentação e o processamento eficaz das transações comerciais.

Funções Essenciais

Estabelecer e manter relações interfuncionais com as partes interessadas internas, bem como construir relações com as partes interessadas externas, em particular os clientes, para recolher documentos e informações relevantes que permitam a realização das atividades necessárias de due diligence e de processamento de transações comerciais, e para se manter a par das decisões e regulamentações comerciais e nacionais.

Compreender as decisões, a legislação, as normas e as práticas bancárias exigidas em matéria de comércio e controlo cambial, e utilizar o bom senso e a interpretação para orientar as verificações de documentação e viabilidade, bem como a aprovação, de modo a permitir o processamento das transações e a mitigar riscos e perdas para o SBG.

Verificar as instruções recebidas de clientes e/ou bancos (incluindo documentos e pedidos dos clientes), validando as informações em relação aos requisitos da solução comercial, e digitalizar as instruções e documentos nos sistemas de fluxo de trabalho relevantes para registar a transação.

Trabalhar em estreita colaboração com equipas multifuncionais para concluir as verificações necessárias (por exemplo, viabilidade, verificações de crédito, verificações de conformidade,

verificações regulamentares), examinando e verificando se foram recebidos os documentos corretos, e garantir que os documentos e informações cumprem os requisitos do produto de transação, bem como quaisquer regulamentos, decisões, leis, normas e práticas bancárias específicas da transação e/ou do país.

documentar, alterar preços) nas instruções de transação, de modo a permitir que a transação seja processada atempadamente e que os detalhes estejam corretos para efeitos de auditoria.

Colaborar com as partes interessadas e os clientes para os manter informados sobre erros identificados e proporcionar formação e sensibilização para evitar que se repitam no futuro.

Cumprir as políticas e procedimentos internos e externos relevantes e respeitar os organismos reguladores para garantir que toda a Due Diligence cumpre as normas exigidas e que o trabalho é realizado de forma controlada e consistente.

Prestar orientação no local de trabalho aos novos membros da equipa para desenvolver capacidades e melhorar competências para o desempenho das tarefas operacionais do dia-a-dia

relacionadas com o Processamento de Transações e a Due Diligence.

Área de estudo: N/A

jobs.title: Director, Manufacturing QA
jobs.description:
Responsible for overall quality of AbbVie products including small molecule pharmaceuticals and/or biologics, combination products, and medical devices—complying with delivery time objectives; local, divisional, and corporate policies; and ext. agency regulations worldwide. Scope of responsibility can also include business processes supporting new product introduction, product monitoring, or post-market quality systems. Products include regulatory starting materials, Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (API), produced by AbbVie or third-party manufacturer Intermediates/Drug Products. Acts as the principle, quality, global supply chain rep. with external manufacturing businesses. Builds and maintains relationships with TPM Operations, TPM Business Alliance, Commercial, Global Supply Chain, Domestic and International AbbVie Plants and Affiliates, Regulatory Affairs, R&D, and S&T to align strategic initiatives. Develop regulatory strategies for brands with Regulatory Affairs. Grade depe

Responsibilities

Develop and lead a quality professional team responsible for assigned products’ transfer activities and end-to-end product quality—conforming to worldwide standards/regulations throughout the NPI supply chain & departmental budget. Lead Product Quality Assurance Transfer Mngr.s to develop strong relationships with Third Party Manufacturers, AbbVie plants, affiliates, & other functional groups. Help them understand each project’s quality, compliance, & org. resource needs; & align roles and res

• Ensure delivery of all quality elements needed to facilitate new product launches including Third Party Manufacturer’s that provide products directly to distribution centers, or to AbbVie domestic and International plants for further manufacturing, packaging and/or testing.
• Core team member or strategic programs lead; including Pipeline Teams, New Product Introductions, Governance Process, CMC Leadership Team, Product Transfers, Specification Approval Team, Regulatory Starting Material Core Team, Global Strategic Sourcing, Due Diligence, and Site Selection. Make primary decisions on product quality, compliance and regulatory conformance issues for sterile, biological, liquid, solids, and/or device products and elevates medium and high risk events to AbbVie mngmnt.
• Develop and implement a global Product Quality Assurance strategy to support quality systems or product requirements associated with pharmaceuticals, biologics, devices and combination products manufactured at AbbVie plants or third party manufacturing (TPM) facilities. Provide a Quality Assurance perspective during new product development and address resolution of quality and compliance issues.
• Support development of the legal supply agreements, contracts and letters of intent to ensure the appropriate quality, compliance, and regulatory aspects are met for the products and services covered. Manage and approve organizations actions—like Quality and Technical agreements— as a representative of AbbVie, within the legal boundaries of these documents. Approves negotiated quality and technical agreement as a representative of AbbVie.
• Key decision maker on product quality, compliance, and regulatory conformance issues for sterile, biological, liquid, solids and/or device products. Complete management reviews with assigned TPMs that identify and address quality, operational, and organizational issues. Interface with Quality Assurance audit team to develop audit plans, due diligence plans, and inspection readiness plans, review audit observations and responses, and maintain corrective action timetable.
• Provide support for quality audits, initial site approvals and due diligence activities. Direct and manage pre-approval inspection readiness as related to the third party manufacturers to ensure regulatory approvals are obtained, with no delays to market entries. Actively participates and interfaces directly/indirectly with the FDA, EMA, MHRA, ANVISA, MoH, etc. for pre-approval inspections.
• Function as main Quality liaison between Third Party Manufacturers (TPMs) and AbbVie Operations in support of commercial operations, new product introductions, and product transfers. Negotiates with external companies’ upper management to maintain a consistent level of quality and a level of expectation that will minimize compliance risks but also balance the cost of operating to provide AbbVie with the agreed service.
• Establish and maintain relationships and open communication with Third Party Manufacturers (TPMs), AbbVie plants, affiliates and other functional groups (R&D, Regulatory, Purchasing, etc.) to define roles and responsibilities and identify potential projects and issues. Obtain an in-depth understanding of the quality, compliance, and resource needs at each transfer site. Provide quality oversight and guidance for successful validations (processes, test methods, etc.) and qualifications.
• Communicate and negotiate with the TPM’s quality organization to maintain a consistent level of quality and a level of expectation that will minimize compliance risks but also balance the cost of operating to provide AbbVie with the agreed service. Prioritize programs, initiatives, and problem solving with consideration for impact to timelines, resources and conflicting priorities.

• Bachelor’s Degree in relevant Life Science, Pharmacy, or Engineering is required. Graduate degree preferred.
• Technical or Analytical background required for problem resolution with technical, quality, product and or engineering related issues.
• Total combined years of experience 15+ years. In the pharmaceutical, biologics, device, or chemical industry—a minimum of 5 years of experience in Manufacturing and 4 years of experience in QA, R&D, and/or S&T. Minimum of 6 years Management and Supervision experience.
• Minimum of 5 years’ experience in a direct Plant pharmaceutical setting role. Required regulatory inspection experience with direct interaction with regulatory inspectors.
• Expert knowledge and a comprehensive understanding of biological and/or pharmaceutical technologies (sterile, biological, liquid, ointments, devices, solid tablets and caplets, suspensions, granulations, soft elastic capsules, gel caps, extended release products, coating solutions, and/or active pharmaceutical ingredients).
• Possesses knowledge and a skill set to operate within an environment that requires a high degree of urgency, positive interpersonal skills, ability to manage multiple complex tasks simultaneously.
• Capable of analyzing data facts and informed opinion to direct the development of effective action plans as well as the ability to problem solve without the benefit of precedent.
• The incumbent must be capable of understanding and overcoming differing cultural and language obstacles to provide solutions that satisfy Corporate, Divisional, regional, and local objectives to effectively manage the action plans that will resolve the issues.
• Strong leadership skills required to manage professional staff and effectively interface with senior leaders both internally as well as with external organizations. Capacity to perform as a leader, team member, and individual.
• Experience with the requirements for third party external manufacturing.
